items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together constitute a great accomplishment.
Such accomplishment can arise for a practitioner.
The yoginīs hold this accomplishment in regard.
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation becomes dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

The ordinal given is the ninth.
items.inference: The ninth chapter, emerged in Candra-dvīpa, is concluded.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self standing on one foot surrounded by fire.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self standing on one foot, surrounded by fire.

items.question: What request is made to the god regarding the determination of knowledge?
premises: A speaker addresses the god directly.
The speaker seeks the determination of knowledge.
The speaker asks for it to be made manifest now.
items.inference: The speaker requests the god to make the determination of knowledge manifest now.
items.plain_english: O God, make the determination of knowledge manifest to me now.

items.question: What division of eight octads is sought to be known exhaustively?
premises: There is a division consisting of eight octads.
The speaker seeks to know this division fully.
The knowing is desired in an exhaustive manner.
items.inference: The speaker seeks to know fully and exhaustively the division of the eight octads.
items.plain_english: I seek to know fully and endlessly the division of the eight octads.

rows.grounds: first member of compound qualifying sthānaṃ

items.question: How is accomplishment quickly attained in the secret wheel, O Bhairava?
premises: A secret place is identified as a wheel.
Accomplishment occurs in relation to this wheel.
The accomplishment is said to happen quickly.
items.inference: In the secret place known as the wheel, accomplishment is attained quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell how accomplishment is quickly attained in the secret place that is the wheel.

rows.grounds: first member of compound describing rarity

items.question: Why does Bhairava praise the goddess for asking a question rare among gods?
premises: Bhairava expresses strong approval to the great goddess.
He states that he has been asked a question.
The matter asked about is hard to obtain even for the gods.
items.inference: Bhairava praises the goddess because she has asked about something rare and hard for the gods to obtain.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess; you have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

rows.grounds: state or identity assigned to kṣakāraṃ

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables kṣa and laṃ?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with a specific state.
That state is identified as brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is located in the forehead.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa corresponds to the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ corresponds to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is morphologically dual though translated as a single region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is the state of the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Which bodily locations are assigned to the syllables ṣa and śa?
premises: The syllable ṣa is placed in a specific bodily region.

The syllable śa is placed in the heart.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa corresponds to the throat region, and the syllable śa corresponds to the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.inference: The meditation object is a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
items.plain_english: Meditate on the divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner abandon after gaining equanimity through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an equal or balanced mind.
A practitioner with such a mind faces a choice of conduct.
Village or conventional duty is named as something to abandon.
items.inference: Through practice, one with an equal mind should abandon conventional village duties.
uncertainties: grāma dharmañ may refer broadly to conventional social duties
items.plain_english: Through practice, becoming even-minded, one should abandon the duties of village life.

premises: The practice yields specific forms of knowledge.

items.inference: The practice grants knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of distant hearing and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are summarized as immortality and transformation?
premises: Additional attainments are being listed.
Immortality is named among them.
Transformation is also named in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the attainments include immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam could imply bodily or state transformation
items.plain_english: O goddess, in brief, one attains immortality and likewise transformation.

items.inference: The second eight-petaled wheel is well illuminated through fiery meditation.
uncertainties: teja may mean fire or radiant energy
items.plain_english: The second is the eight-petaled wheel, well illuminated by meditation on radiant fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?

items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can assume many forms.

premises: The practitioner may become angry.

items.plain_english: But when angry, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.plain_english: It brings the destruction of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.inference: In solitude, one intent on meditation should manifest form in many ways.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, make yourself appear in many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice of this discipline?

items.inference: One devoted to constant practice indeed attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.plain_english: By not eating day after day, one will indeed go to death through the decline of age.

items.question: What power arises from continually contemplating a smoke-colored triple world?
premises: The practitioner contemplates something smoke-colored.
The contemplation is directed toward the triple world.
